column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|06-09|68|Νέρων|Nero|Nero was Roman emperor from 54 to 68. During his reign the Great Fire of Rome broke out in 64, for which he was blamed, and he blamed the Christians. He lost the support of the army and took his own life in 68.

bio|06-09|1672|Μέγας Πέτρος|Peter the Great|Peter the Great was tsar and, from 1721, emperor of Russia. He modernised the state on Western models, created a navy, built Saint Petersburg and defeated Sweden in the Great Northern War. He died in 1725.

bio|06-09|1843|Μπέρτα φον Ζούτνερ|Bertha von Suttner|Bertha von Suttner was an Austrian writer and pacifist. She wrote the anti-war novel "Lay Down Your Arms!" and in 1905 became the first woman to be awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|06-09|1870|Κάρολος Ντίκενς|Charles Dickens|Charles Dickens died in 1870 and was buried in Westminster Abbey. He was the greatest English novelist of the Victorian era, with works such as "Oliver Twist" and "Great Expectations".

bio|06-09|1963|Τζόνι Ντεπ|Johnny Depp|Johnny Depp is an American actor. He became known as Jack Sparrow in "Pirates of the Caribbean" and in films by Tim Burton, such as "Edward Scissorhands". He has been nominated three times for an Oscar.

bio|06-09|1974|Μιγκέλ Άνχελ Αστούριας|Miguel Ángel Asturias|Miguel Ángel Asturias was a Guatemalan writer and diplomat. He wrote the novel "Mr. President" about a dictatorship. In 1967 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-09|1978|Μίροσλαβ Κλόζε|Miroslav Klose|Miroslav Klose is a former German footballer of Polish origin. He is the top scorer in the history of the knockout stages of the World Cups, with 16 goals, and he won the 2014 World Cup.

bio|06-09|1981|Νάταλι Πόρτμαν|Natalie Portman|Natalie Portman was born in Israel and grew up in the United States. She is an actress and won the Academy Award for Best Actress for "Black Swan". She also appeared in the "Star Wars" films and in "V for Vendetta".

bio|06-09|1994|Γιαν Τίνμπεργκεν|Jan Tinbergen|Jan Tinbergen was a Dutch economist. He developed mathematical models for the economy and in 1969 became, together with Ragnar Frisch, the first to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics.

bio|06-10|1819|Γκυστάβ Κουρμπέ|Gustave Courbet|Gustave Courbet was a French painter and leader of realism. He painted everyday people and scenes, such as "The Stonebreakers" and "A Burial at Ornans". He took part in the Paris Commune.

bio|06-10|1836|Αντρέ Μαρί Αμπέρ|André-Marie Ampère|André-Marie Ampère was a French physicist and mathematician. He developed the theory of electromagnetism, and the unit of electric current, the ampere, is named after him. He died in Marseille in 1836.

bio|06-10|1915|Σολ Μπέλοου|Saul Bellow|Saul Bellow was born in Canada and lived in Chicago. He was a writer and wrote "The Adventures of Augie March" and "Humboldt's Gift". In 1976 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-10|1921|Φίλιππος|Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh|Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, was born in Corfu as a prince of Greece and Denmark. In 1947 he married Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom. He became the longest-serving consort of a British monarch and died in 2021.

bio|06-10|1922|Τζούντι Γκάρλαντ|Judy Garland|Judy Garland was an American actress and singer. She became known as Dorothy in "The Wizard of Oz" in 1939, where she sang "Over the Rainbow". She was the mother of Liza Minnelli.

bio|06-10|1926|Αντόνι Γκαουντί|Antoni Gaudí|Antoni Gaudí was a Catalan architect. He became known for his distinctive organic style, with works such as the Sagrada Família in Barcelona and Park Güell. He died in 1926 after being struck by a tram.

bio|06-10|1949|Σίγκριντ Ούντσετ|Sigrid Undset|Sigrid Undset died in 1949. She was a Norwegian writer and wrote the novel "Kristin Lavransdatter", about the Middle Ages. In 1928 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-10|1959|Κάρλο Αντσελότι|Carlo Ancelotti|Carlo Ancelotti is an Italian coach and former footballer. As a coach he has won the Champions League five times, with Milan and Real Madrid, and league titles in many countries.

bio|06-10|2004|Ρέι Τσαρλς|Ray Charles|Ray Charles was an American singer and pianist. Blind from childhood, he combined soul, gospel and jazz, and wrote hits such as "Georgia on My Mind". His life became the film "Ray".

bio|06-11|1859|Κλέμενς φον Μέττερνιχ|Klemens von Metternich|Klemens von Metternich died in 1859 in Vienna. He was an Austrian politician and foreign minister, and the architect of the Congress of Vienna in 1815, and he opposed national and liberal movements.

bio|06-11|1864|Ρίχαρντ Στράους|Richard Strauss|Richard Strauss was a German composer and conductor. He wrote the symphonic poems "Thus Spoke Zarathustra" and "Don Juan", and the operas "Salome" and "The Knight of the Rose".

bio|06-11|1899|Γιασουνάρι Καβαμπάτα|Yasunari Kawabata|Yasunari Kawabata was a Japanese writer. He wrote "Snow Country" and "The Sound of the Mountain". In 1968 he became the first Japanese to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-11|1910|Ζακ-Ιβ Κουστώ|Jacques-Yves Cousteau|Jacques-Yves Cousteau was a French oceanographer and explorer. He contributed to the invention of the aqualung for underwater diving and made documentaries, such as "The Silent World". He sailed on the ship "Calypso".

bio|06-11|1933|Τζιν Γουάιλντερ|Gene Wilder|Gene Wilder was an American actor and comedian. He became known through the films of Mel Brooks, "The Producers" and "Young Frankenstein", and as Willy Wonka in "Willy Wonka".

bio|06-11|1934|Λεβ Βιγκότσκι|Lev Vygotsky|Lev Vygotsky was a Soviet psychologist. He developed the theory of the "zone of proximal development" and argued for the social role in children's cognitive development. He died young, at the age of 37.

bio|06-11|1969|Πίτερ Ντίνκλατζ|Peter Dinklage|Peter Dinklage is an American actor. He became famous for the role of Tyrion Lannister in the series "Game of Thrones", for which he won several Emmy Awards.

bio|06-11|1970|Αλέξανδρος Κερένσκι|Alexander Kerensky|Alexander Kerensky died in 1970 in New York. He was head of the Russian Provisional Government in 1917 and was overthrown by the Bolsheviks. He spent the rest of his life in exile.
bio|06-11|1979|Τζον Γουέιν|John Wayne|John Wayne died in 1979 of cancer. He was an American actor and the best-known star of the Western, with films such as "Train of Terror" and "The Searchers".

bio|06-12|1890|Έγκον Σίλε|Egon Schiele|Egon Schiele was an Austrian painter of Expressionism and a pupil of Klimt. He became known for his intense portraits and nudes. He died young, at the age of 28, from the flu of 1918.
bio|06-12|1897|Άντονι Ήντεν|Anthony Eden|Anthony Eden was a British Conservative politician. He was foreign secretary and prime minister from 1955 to 1957, when he resigned after the Suez Crisis.

bio|06-12|1912|Φρεντερίκ Πασσύ|Frédéric Passy|Frédéric Passy was a French economist and pacifist. He founded one of the first peace organisations, and in 1901 became the first to be awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, together with Henry Dunant.

bio|06-12|1924|Τζορτζ Μπους|George H. W. Bush|George H. W. Bush was the 41st president of the United States, from 1989 to 1993. He fought as a pilot in the Second World War, was director of the CIA and vice president under Reagan. During his term the Gulf War took place.

bio|06-12|1929|Άννα Φρανκ|Anne Frank|Anne Frank was born in Frankfurt. As a Jew, she hid with her family in Amsterdam during the Second World War and kept a diary. She was arrested in 1944 and died in Bergen-Belsen in 1945. Her diary was published by her father.

bio|06-12|1983|Νόρμα Σίρερ|Norma Shearer|Norma Shearer was a Canadian actress in Hollywood. She won the Academy Award for Best Actress for "The Divorcee", and she was one of the most important stars of the 1930s.

bio|06-12|1992|Φιλίπε Κουτίνιο|Philippe Coutinho|Philippe Coutinho is a Brazilian footballer. He played as a midfielder for Liverpool, Barcelona and the Brazilian national team. He was known for his dribbles and his shots.

bio|06-12|2003|Γκρέγκορι Πεκ|Gregory Peck|Gregory Peck died in 2003. He was an American actor who won an Oscar for "To Kill a Mockingbird", where he played the lawyer Atticus Finch. He also appeared in "Roman Holiday".

bio|06-12|2006|Γκιέργκι Λίγκετι|György Ligeti|György Ligeti was a Hungarian composer. He wrote pioneering works with dense textures of sound, such as "Atmosphères", which is heard in the film "2001: A Space Odyssey".

bio|06-13|1831|Τζέιμς Κλαρκ Μάξγουελ|James Clerk Maxwell|James Clerk Maxwell was a Scottish physicist. He formulated Maxwell's equations, which unified electricity, magnetism and light as electromagnetic waves, and he is regarded as one of the greatest physicists.

bio|06-13|1865|Ουίλιαμ Μπάτλερ Γέιτς|William Butler Yeats|William Butler Yeats was born in Dublin. He was a poet and playwright and a central figure of the Irish literary revival. In 1923 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-13|1886|Λουδοβίκος Β΄|Ludwig II|Ludwig II was king of Bavaria from 1864. He was a supporter of Wagner and built castles such as Neuschwanstein. He was declared unfit to reign and died in 1886 in Lake Starnberg, in unclear circumstances.

bio|06-13|1888|Φερνάντο Πεσσόα|Fernando Pessoa|Fernando Pessoa was a Portuguese poet. He wrote under many heteronyms, with different names and personalities, such as Álvaro de Campos and Ricardo Reis. "The Book of Disquiet" was published after his death.

bio|06-13|1928|Τζων Φορμπς Νας|John Forbes Nash|John Forbes Nash was an American mathematician. He developed the "Nash equilibrium" in game theory, and in 1994 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics. His life became the film "A Beautiful Mind".

bio|06-13|1938|Σαρλ Εντουάρ Γκιγιόμ|Charles Édouard Guillaume|Charles Édouard Guillaume died in 1938. He was a Swiss physicist who discovered the alloys Invar and Elinvar, which do not expand with temperature. In 1920 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.
bio|06-13|1944|Μπαν Κι-μουν|Ban Ki-moon|Ban Ki-moon is a South Korean diplomat and politician. He was the eighth Secretary-General of the United Nations, from 2007 to 2016.

bio|06-13|1965|Μάρτιν Μπούμπερ|Martin Buber|Martin Buber was a Jewish philosopher born in Vienna. He wrote "I and Thou", a work on the relationship of humans with God and with others. He moved to Palestine in 1938.

bio|06-13|1982|Χαλίντ|Khalid|Khalid was king of Saudi Arabia from 1975, when Faisal was assassinated, until 1982. During his reign the Grand Mosque of Mecca was seized in 1979, and oil revenues increased.

bio|06-14|1736|Σαρλ Ογκυστέν ντε Κουλόμπ|Charles-Augustin de Coulomb|Charles-Augustin de Coulomb was a French physicist. He formulated Coulomb's law for the electric force between charges. The unit of electric charge, the coulomb, is named after him.

bio|06-14|1811|Χάριετ Μπίτσερ Στόου|Harriet Beecher Stowe|Harriet Beecher Stowe was an American writer. She wrote "Uncle Tom's Cabin", an anti-slavery work of 1852 that had enormous influence and contributed to the rupture that led to the Civil War.

bio|06-14|1837|Τζάκομο Λεοπάρντι|Giacomo Leopardi|Giacomo Leopardi was an Italian poet and philologist. He wrote the "Canti", with poems such as "The Infinite", and many philosophical works in a pessimistic tone. He was an outstanding philologist and died young, at the age of 38.

bio|06-14|1920|Μαξ Βέμπερ|Max Weber|Max Weber was a German sociologist and economist. He wrote "The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism" and developed concepts about bureaucracy and authority. He died in 1920.

bio|06-14|1928|Τσε Γκεβάρα|Che Guevara|Ernesto "Che" Guevara was born in Argentina and studied medicine. He took part in the Cuban Revolution with Fidel Castro and later led guerrillas in Bolivia, where he was killed in 1967. He became a symbol of the revolutionary left.

bio|06-14|1946|Ντόναλντ Τραμπ|Donald Trump|Donald Trump is an American businessman and Republican politician. He was the 45th president of the United States from 2017 to 2021 and was elected again in 2024 as the 47th president.

bio|06-14|1968|Σαλβατόρε Κουαζίμοντο|Salvatore Quasimodo|Salvatore Quasimodo was an Italian poet. He was one of the main representatives of hermeticism, and in 1959 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-14|1969|Στέφι Γκραφ|Steffi Graf|Steffi Graf is a former German tennis player. She won 22 Grand Slam tournaments, and in 1988 she achieved the "Golden Slam", winning all four and the Olympic gold medal in the same year.

bio|06-14|1986|Χόρχε Λουίς Μπόρχες|Jorge Luis Borges|Jorge Luis Borges was an Argentine writer. He wrote stories and poems, such as "Fictions" and "The Aleph", with themes such as time, labyrinths and dreams. In his last years he was blind.

bio|06-15|1843|Έντβαρντ Γκρηγκ|Edvard Grieg|Edvard Grieg was a Norwegian Romantic composer. He wrote the music for "Peer Gynt", including the pieces "Morning" and "In the Hall of the Mountain King", as well as a piano concerto.

bio|06-15|1849|Τζέιμς Νοξ Πολκ|James Knox Polk|James Knox Polk died in 1849. He was the 11th president of the United States, from 1845 to 1849. During his presidency the war with Mexico took place and the United States acquired large territories, such as California. He died a few months after his term ended.

bio|06-15|1888|Φρειδερίκος Γ΄|Frederick III|Frederick III was German emperor and king of Prussia for only 99 days in 1888. He was a liberal, but he already had cancer of the larynx when he came to the throne. He was succeeded by his son Wilhelm II.

bio|06-15|1889|Μιχαήλ Εμινέσκου|Mihai Eminescu|Mihai Eminescu was a Romanian poet and is regarded as the national poet of Romania. He wrote "Luceafărul" and "The Ode", and he died young in 1889, at the age of 39.

bio|06-15|1914|Γιούρι Αντρόπωφ|Yuri Andropov|Yuri Andropov was a Soviet politician. He led the KGB for many years and succeeded Brezhnev as general secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union in 1982. He died after 15 months in power.

bio|06-15|1953|Σι Τσινπίνγκ|Xi Jinping|Xi Jinping is a Chinese politician. Since 2012 he has been general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party, and since 2013 president of China. In 2018 the limit on the terms of the president was abolished.

bio|06-15|1992|Μοχάμεντ Σαλάχ|Mohamed Salah|Mohamed Salah is an Egyptian footballer. He played for Roma and Liverpool, where he became one of the leading scorers, and he won the Champions League in 2019. He is a hero of the Egyptian national team.

bio|06-15|1996|Έλλα Φιτζέραλντ|Ella Fitzgerald|Ella Fitzgerald was an American jazz singer. She had a voice of great range and was skilled in scat singing, and she won 13 Grammy Awards. She was called "the First Lady of Song".

bio|06-16|1723|Άνταμ Σμιθ|Adam Smith|Adam Smith was a Scottish philosopher and economist. In "The Wealth of Nations" of 1776 he analysed the division of labour and the "invisible hand" of the market. He is regarded as the father of classical economics.

bio|06-16|1829|Τζερόνιμο|Geronimo|Geronimo was a leader of the Chiricahua Apache and the chief of their warriors. He resisted the American and Mexican armies for years, until he surrendered in 1886. He died in 1909 as a prisoner of war.
bio|06-16|1890|Σταν Λόρελ|Stan Laurel|Stan Laurel was an English comedian. With Oliver Hardy he formed the duo Laurel and Hardy in silent and sound films, known in Greek as "The Fat and the Thin".

bio|06-16|1958|Ίμρε Νάγκυ|Imre Nagy|Imre Nagy was a Hungarian politician. He became prime minister and led the Hungarian Uprising of 1956 against Soviet domination. After its suppression he was arrested and executed in 1958.

bio|06-16|1967|Γιούργκεν Κλοπ|Jürgen Klopp|Jürgen Klopp is a German football coach. He won league titles with Borussia Dortmund and with Liverpool, with which he also won the Champions League in 2019.

bio|06-16|1971|Τούπακ Σακούρ|Tupac Shakur|Tupac Shakur was an American rapper and actor. He was one of the most successful and influential hip-hop artists, with songs such as "Changes". He was shot and died in 1996, at the age of 25.

bio|06-16|1977|Βέρνερ φον Μπράουν|Wernher von Braun|Wernher von Braun died in 1977. He was a German engineer who developed the V-2 rockets, and after the war he worked for NASA, where he led the development of the Saturn V rocket.
bio|06-16|1991|Τζιν Άρθουρ|Jean Arthur|Jean Arthur was an American actress. She became famous for the comedies of Frank Capra, such as "Mr. Deeds Goes to Town" and "Mr. Smith Goes to Washington".

bio|06-16|2017|Χέλμουτ Κολ|Helmut Kohl|Helmut Kohl died in 2017. He was chancellor of Germany from 1982 to 1998 and led the country's reunification in 1990. He was a strong supporter of European integration.

bio|06-17|1239|Εδουάρδος Α΄|Edward I|Edward I was king of England from 1272 to 1307. He conquered Wales and fought the Scots. He carried out legal reforms and was known as "Longshanks" and the "Hammer of the Scots".

bio|06-17|1682|Κάρολος ΙΒ΄|Charles XII|Charles XII was king of Sweden from 1697 to 1718. He was a capable general, but he was defeated by Peter the Great at Poltava in 1709. He was killed in 1718 in Norway.
bio|06-17|1696|Γιαν Σομπιέσκι|Jan III Sobieski|Jan III Sobieski was king of Poland from 1674. He became known for leading the army that saved Vienna from the Ottomans in 1683. He died in 1696.

bio|06-17|1719|Τζόζεφ Άντισον|Joseph Addison|Joseph Addison died in 1719. He was an English writer and politician who, together with Richard Steele, published the periodicals "The Tatler" and "The Spectator".

bio|06-17|1882|Ιγκόρ Στραβίνσκι|Igor Stravinsky|Igor Stravinsky was a Russian composer who lived in France and the United States. He wrote the ballets "The Firebird", "Petrushka" and "The Rite of Spring", which changed the music of the 20th century.

bio|06-17|1898|Μαουρίτς Κορνέλις Έσερ|M. C. Escher|M. C. Escher was a Dutch graphic artist. He became known for his works with optical illusions and mathematical symmetries, such as "Ascending and Descending".

bio|06-17|1942|Μοχάμεντ Ελ Μπαραντέι|Mohamed ElBaradei|Mohamed ElBaradei is an Egyptian diplomat. He was director general of the International Atomic Energy Agency from 1997 to 2009, and in 2005 he shared the Nobel Peace Prize with the agency.

bio|06-17|1996|Τόμας Κουν|Thomas Kuhn|Thomas Kuhn was an American philosopher and historian of science. In his work "The Structure of Scientific Revolutions" he introduced the concepts of the "paradigm" and of "scientific revolutions".
bio|06-17|2015|Σουλεϊμάν Ντεμιρέλ|Süleyman Demirel|Süleyman Demirel was a Turkish politician. He was several times prime minister, and from 1993 to 2000 he was president of Turkey.

bio|06-18|1928|Ρόαλντ Αμούνδσεν|Roald Amundsen|Roald Amundsen was a Norwegian explorer. In 1911 he led the first expedition that reached the South Pole, and later he explored the Arctic. He disappeared in 1928 during a rescue mission by aircraft.

bio|06-18|1929|Γιούργκεν Χάμπερμας|Jürgen Habermas|Jürgen Habermas was born in Düsseldorf, Germany. He was a philosopher and sociologist, a representative of the second generation of the Frankfurt School, and he wrote about the "theory of communicative action" and the public sphere.
bio|06-18|1936|Μαξίμ Γκόρκι|Maxim Gorky|Maxim Gorky died in 1936. He was a Russian writer and is regarded as the founder of socialist realism. He wrote "The Mother" and "The Lower Depths".

bio|06-18|1942|Πολ Μακάρτνεϊ|Paul McCartney|Paul McCartney is an English musician, bassist and songwriter of the Beatles. He wrote songs with John Lennon such as "Yesterday" and "Hey Jude", and he went on with Wings and as a solo artist.

bio|06-18|1949|Λεχ Κατσίνσκι|Lech Kaczyński|Lech Kaczyński was a Polish politician and the twin brother of Jarosław. He was mayor of Warsaw and from 2005 president of Poland. He was killed in 2010 in an air crash at Smolensk.

bio|06-18|1949|Γιαροσλάβ Κατσίνσκι|Jarosław Kaczyński|Jarosław Kaczyński is a Polish politician, founder and leader of the Law and Justice party. He was prime minister of Poland in 2006 and 2007. He is the twin brother of Lech Kaczyński.
bio|06-18|1952|Ιντρίς Ντεμπί|Idriss Déby|Idriss Déby was a military officer and president of Chad from 1990 to 2021. He came to power in a coup and ruled for about three decades.

bio|06-18|1974|Γκεόργκι Ζούκοφ|Georgy Zhukov|Georgy Zhukov was a marshal of the Soviet Union. He led important victories in the Second World War, such as the Battle of Moscow and the capture of Berlin in 1945. He died in 1974.

bio|06-18|2010|Ζοζέ Σαραμάγκου|José Saramago|José Saramago was a Portuguese writer. He wrote the novels "Blindness", "The Gospel According to Jesus Christ" and "The Error of Ricardo Reis". In 1998 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-19|1566|Ιάκωβος Α΄|James I|James I was king of Scotland as James VI and from 1603 king of England, uniting the two crowns. He was the father of Charles I and commissioned the "King James Bible".

bio|06-19|1623|Μπλεζ Πασκάλ|Blaise Pascal|Blaise Pascal was a French mathematician, physicist and philosopher. He built one of the first calculating machines and wrote the "Pensées" and the "Provincial Letters". The unit of pressure, the pascal, is named after him.

bio|06-19|1867|Μαξιμιλιανός Α΄|Maximilian I|Maximilian I was an Austrian archduke and emperor of Mexico from 1864. He had been installed by Napoleon III of France. When France withdrew, he was captured by the republicans of Juárez and executed in 1867.
bio|06-19|1937|Τζέιμς Μάθιου Μπάρι|J. M. Barrie|J. M. Barrie died in 1937. He was a Scottish writer and playwright who created "Peter Pan", first as a play in 1904.

bio|06-19|1945|Αούνγκ Σαν Σου Κι|Aung San Suu Kyi|Aung San Suu Kyi is a Burmese politician and leader of the opposition in Burma (Myanmar). She was under house arrest for 15 years, and in 1991 she was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. After the military coup of 2021 she was arrested.

bio|06-19|1945|Ράντοβαν Κάρατζιτς|Radovan Karadžić|Radovan Karadžić is a Serbian psychiatrist and politician. He was president of the Bosnian Serb Republic during the war of the 1990s. He was convicted by the International Court in The Hague of genocide and war crimes.

bio|06-19|1964|Μπόρις Τζόνσον|Boris Johnson|Boris Johnson is a British Conservative politician. He was mayor of London and foreign secretary, and from 2019 to 2022 he was prime minister of the United Kingdom, when Brexit took place.

bio|06-19|1993|Ουίλιαμ Γκόλντινγκ|William Golding|William Golding was an English writer. He wrote the novel "Lord of the Flies", about a group of boys on a deserted island. In 1983 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
bio|06-19|2013|Τζέιμς Γκαντολφίνι|James Gandolfini|James Gandolfini was an American actor. He became famous for the role of Tony Soprano in "The Sopranos", for which he won three Emmy Awards.

bio|06-20|840|Λουδοβίκος ο Ευσεβής|Louis the Pious|Louis the Pious was king of the Franks and emperor from 814, son and heir of Charlemagne. His reign was marked by conflicts with his sons over the succession. He died in 840.

bio|06-20|1580|Λουίς δε Καμόες|Luís de Camões|Luís de Camões was a Portuguese poet. He wrote the epic "The Lusiads", about the voyages of the Portuguese, and poems about love. He is regarded as the national poet of Portugal.

bio|06-20|1819|Ζακ Οφενμπάχ|Jacques Offenbach|Jacques Offenbach was born in Germany and lived in Paris. He was a composer and created the genre of operetta. He wrote "Orpheus in the Underworld" and the opera "The Tales of Hoffmann".

bio|06-20|1837|Γουλιέλμος Δ΄|William IV|William IV was king of the United Kingdom from 1830 to 1837. During his reign the Reform Act of 1832 was passed and slavery was abolished in the empire. He was succeeded by his niece Victoria.

bio|06-20|1928|Μάρτιν Λαντάου|Martin Landau|Martin Landau was an American actor. He won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor for "Ed Wood", where he played Bela Lugosi, and he appeared in the series "Mission: Impossible".

bio|06-20|1928|Ζαν-Μαρί Λε Πεν|Jean-Marie Le Pen|Jean-Marie Le Pen was a French far-right politician. He founded the National Front in 1972 and caused a surprise by reaching the second round of the presidential elections of 2002. He was the father of Marine Le Pen.

bio|06-20|1966|Ζωρζ Λεμαίτρ|Georges Lemaître|Georges Lemaître was a Belgian priest, physicist and astronomer. In 1927 he proposed that the universe is expanding, and in 1931 he put forward the idea of the "primeval atom", a forerunner of the Big Bang theory.
bio|06-20|1967|Νικόλ Κίντμαν|Nicole Kidman|Nicole Kidman is an Australian actress. She won the Academy Award for Best Actress for "The Hours" and appeared in "Moulin Rouge!" and "Big Little Lies".

bio|06-20|1978|Φρανκ Λάμπαρντ|Frank Lampard|Frank Lampard is a former English footballer. He played as a midfielder for Chelsea and for the England national team, and he is Chelsea's all-time top scorer. He later became a coach.

bio|06-21|1527|Νικολό Μακιαβέλι|Niccolò Machiavelli|Niccolò Machiavelli died in 1527 in Florence. He was an Italian politician and thinker who wrote "The Prince", a work on the exercise of power with realism.

bio|06-21|1905|Ζαν-Πολ Σαρτρ|Jean-Paul Sartre|Jean-Paul Sartre was a French philosopher and writer and a central figure of existentialism. He wrote "Being and Nothingness" and the novel "Nausea". In 1964 he declined the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|06-21|1908|Νικολάι Ρίμσκι-Κόρσακοφ|Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov|Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov was a Russian composer and a member of "The Mighty Handful". He wrote "Scheherazade" and "The Flight of the Bumblebee", and was the teacher of Stravinsky and an expert in orchestration.
